title: 5G NR LDPC GPU kernel tuning to real-time decode rate
description:
## Goal

Tune the GPU LDPC BP kernel (from Phase B `a930be7f`) for the 5G NR
base graphs and per-`i_LS` shift tables until a concrete real-time
decode-rate target is met on gfx1030 for at least one configuration.

**Concrete target (decided 2026-06-07 post-audit per user-approved
Q2)**: BG1, `i_LS` = 1 (Z = 384), rate 1/2, single layer, BLER target
10⁻², decoded transport-block throughput **≥ 200 Mbps** on gfx1030,
measured at the canonical 3GPP NR numerology μ = 1 (30 kHz SCS,
14 OFDM symbols per slot, 273 PRBs). The 200 Mbps figure is the
research-grade bar above DVB-T2 by ~50× and within gfx1030's RDNA2
~16 TFLOPS / 512 GB/s envelope per the adversarial-review
feasibility analysis.

## Context

Task under story `a5635da5` (5G NR + research enablers) within epic
`gf2-sim` (`f9717e7e`). Phase 0 design doc:
`dev/active/ec530af9-pipeline-design.md` §6 (multi-arch dispatch),
§10 (precision). Sequencing: depends on `e478daa8` (and transitively
on `acf9b11a` for the 5G NR base graphs + per-`i_LS` shift tables).
This is the headline benchmark for the epic.

The flat GPU LDPC BP kernel already exists from Phase B `a930be7f`
and is **standard-agnostic** (it decodes any expanded Tanner graph).
Per the `a930be7f` 2026-06-09b amendment (user-approved), the
per-`i_LS` shift table is consumed by the **host-side
`LdpcGraphLayout` builder**, not an in-kernel parameter. This task
therefore builds the 5G NR flat layout by host-expanding base graph +
per-`i_LS` shift table, reuses the existing kernel binary unchanged,
tunes the launch parameters, and measures. **This task also discharges
the full per-`i_LS` shift criterion deferred from `a930be7f`**: it
proves the host-side base+shift→flat-layout path + the flat kernel
reproduce the CPU 5G NR decoder bit-for-bit (see the byte-identity
criterion below).

## Deliverables

1. Tuning sweep harness in
   `crates/gf2-sim/benches/nr_5g_realtime.rs`:
   - Sweeps `batch_size ∈ {64, 128, 256, 512, 1024}`,
     `max_iters ∈ {10, 15, 20, 25}` for the canonical
     configuration (BG1, `i_LS` = 1, Z = 384, rate 1/2, AWGN at
     BLER ≈ 10⁻²).
   - Measures decoded TB throughput (Mbps) and BLER per cell.
   - Selects the highest-throughput cell that still meets BLER
     ≤ 10⁻².
2. Receipt note at `dev/benchmarks/gf2-sim/5g-nr-realtime.md`:
   - Hardware: gfx1030 model, driver, ROCm version, CPU host info.
   - Configuration: full spec of the chosen (BG, `i_LS`, Z, rate,
     decoder algorithm, max_iters, batch_size).
   - Target throughput vs spec PRB throughput (TS 38.214
     reference: μ = 1, 273 PRBs, 1 layer, MCS index implied by
     rate; spec throughput ≈ 459 Mbps for r1/2 + QPSK or
     ≈ 920 Mbps for 16-QAM single-layer — we target ≥ 200 Mbps
     decoded LDPC TB throughput as the [hard] floor; the receipt
     records both spec and observed values).
   - Observed throughput in Mbps with σ over 5 repetitions.
3. Parallelism-pays receipt cross-reference: add an entry to
   `dev/benchmarks/gf2-sim/parallelism-receipts.md` linking to
   the `5g-nr-realtime.md` measurement.
4. **Host-side 5G NR flat-layout builder** (the deferred `a930be7f`
   shift-table consumption point): a constructor that expands a 5G NR
   base graph + per-`i_LS` shift table (from `acf9b11a`) into the flat
   `LdpcGraphLayout` the existing GPU kernel decodes, with NO kernel
   change. Plus a GPU-vs-CPU byte-identity test on a real 5G NR lifted
   code (e.g. the canonical BG1, `i_LS` = 1, Z = 384, rate 1/2) at a
   fixed seed: GPU hard-decision output equals the CPU 5G NR
   `LdpcDecoder` output bit-for-bit.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] At least one (BG, lifting set, rate) configuration meets
  the concrete target: BG1, `i_LS` = 1 (Z = 384), rate 1/2, BLER
  ≤ 10⁻², decoded TB throughput ≥ 200 Mbps on gfx1030.
- [hard] **Per-`i_LS` shift consumption fulfilled (deferred from
  `a930be7f` per its 2026-06-09b amendment, user-directed
  "fulfil the full criterion later"):** the host-side builder expands
  base graph + per-`i_LS` shift table into the flat `LdpcGraphLayout`,
  and the existing flat GPU kernel (reused unchanged) decodes a real
  5G NR lifted code byte-identically to the CPU 5G NR `LdpcDecoder`
  (bit-for-bit hard decision at a fixed seed). This proves the
  "same kernel parameterises both standards" contract end-to-end.
- [hard] Receipt at `dev/benchmarks/gf2-sim/5g-nr-realtime.md`
  records full configuration, target throughput, observed
  throughput (5-rep mean ± σ), and spec PRB throughput comparison
  per TS 38.214 μ = 1, 273 PRBs.
- [hard] `parallelism-pays` gate cross-references the receipt
  with PASS verdict.
- [hard] `cargo-ci`, `code-review`, `parallelism-pays` gates green.

## Non-goals

- Multi-rate / multi-`i_LS` coverage beyond the headline
  configuration (E.4 comparison harness covers additional points
  as desired).
- Multi-GPU / multi-layer MIMO (epic non-goal).
- Real-time end-to-end pipeline including RF impairments (out of
  scope; this task measures decoder throughput only).

## AMENDMENT 2026-06-12 (user-approved): i_LS label correction

Every "`i_LS` = 8" in this issue (and the epic table it mirrors) was a
label bug: lifting-set indices run 0..7 per TS 38.212 Table 5.3.2-1,
and Z = 384 belongs to set `i_LS` = 1 ({3, 6, 12, 24, 48, 96, 192,
384}; `lifting_set_index(384) == 1`). All occurrences above are
corrected to `i_LS` = 1. Pure label fix — Z = 384, rate 1/2, BLER
<= 1e-2, >= 200 Mbps are all unchanged. Same mislabel class the
e478daa8 AMENDMENT 2026-06-09 corrected for its doctest.
